speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with acute diarrhea; to determine the cause, how long have your symptoms been lasting and have you experienced any fever or blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Antibiotic-associated colitis (Clostridioides difficile infection).

The patient's recent treatment with levofloxacin for pneumonia, combined with high-frequency watery diarrhea and cramping, strongly suggests C. diff. I will now request the results of a C. difficile toxin assay and a stool culture to confirm the diagnosis.
